prediction.likelyOutcome: Windsor is the likely net winner: Speedy's $66,000 contract/lien claims are weak given documented ~20% completion, missed deadlines, and work that had to be entirely redone, while Windsor's counterclaim for the $44,300 it paid for worthless work is well supported. The slander-of-title claim adds real but uncertain upside limited mainly to the $3,960 bonding cost absent stronger proof tying the specific interest-rate increase to the lien.

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court found for Windsor, awarded it $44,300 (the amount it had paid Speedy) plus prejudgment and postjudgment interest on its breach-of-contract counterclaim and $3,960 on its slander-of-title counterclaim (bond premiums), a total of $48,260, voided Speedy's $66,000 mechanics lien and denied Speedy's claims. The Second District affirmed.
